decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with vertical through contacts extend the firm's core packaging-wafer competence, and with industry turnover growing, performance likely meets aspiration, so management has no trigger for problemistic search.
Carrier wafers for handling smaller wafers fit the firm's strategic push into reusable carriers and thin-wafer handling, use existing processes at low cost and are probably meeting expectations.

The Cu-interposer was launched prominently at SEMICON Europa and matches the trend toward multifunctional packaging wafers; given the long qualification cycles in semiconductor markets, slack from a growing industry lets the firm carry it while results are still uncertain.
The Wafer Universe off-the-shelf brand uses existing standard production with low incremental cost and widens market reach, so it is unlikely to fall below aspiration in a strong market.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core business and the most likely to fall short of aspiration, but they build on through-glass via know-how, and current slack makes it plausible to keep them a while longer rather than redirect resources now.
